title: L4 Mid-Review: Safe and Sound
story: Your code is now safe from TWO angles: contracts guarantee correctness, ownership guarantees memory safety. Build a mini banking system that proves you've mastered both.
why: This capstone exercise integrates every L4 concept — contracts, ownership, borrowing, invariants, and move semantics — into a real, working system.
analogy: This banking system is a vault — contracts are the combination lock (only valid operations), ownership is the steel walls (no unauthorized access).
try_it: Add fn fn 'total_balance' that takes &Vec[Account] and sums all balances. Then add fn 'richest' that finds the account with the highest balance.
tips: The invariant balance >= 0.0 guarantees no account can go negative
transfer reuses deposit and withdraw — compose small safe functions into larger safe ones
report only needs & — it doesn't modify, so multiple reports can run simultaneously
Every function's signature tells you everything: requires = what it needs, &/&mut = how it accesses
common_mistakes: Forgetting that withdraw's requires prevents overdraft — the invariant alone isn't enough
Using owned parameters for report when & works — unnecessarily consumes the Account
Not adding ensures to deposit and withdraw — the contracts should verify the math
